claim: For every finite field \(\mathbb F_q\), the 15-dimensional truncated free associative algebra \(A=\mathbb F_q\langle x,y\rangle/(x,y)^4\) has exactly \(q^9\) elements whose additive adjoint has rank \(0\), \((q^2-1)q^9\) of rank \(1\), \((q^4-q^2)q^9\) of rank \(2\), and \((q^2-1)q^{13}\) of rank \(4\); rank \(3\) never occurs. The rank-one noncentral locus is exactly the set whose linear part vanishes and whose nonzero quadratic part is a scalar multiple of the square of a linear form. Hence the commuting probability is \(2q^{-4}+q^{-5}-q^{-6}-q^{-7}\), in every characteristic.

correctness.rationale: Homogeneous block proof derives ranks 0,1,2,4 and exact multiplicities for any field; rank-one iff the quadratic part is a nonzero scalar square. Counting centralizers proves the probability. The 15x15 matrix rank checker exhaustively checks q=2,3 patterns and 3000 random full inputs in q=2,3,5.
